summary: Adds a third user-facing domain to FoodTracker: entry management. Provides an Entries screen that lists all stored meal rows from foodtracker.food_logs, with row-level delete (with confirmation), copy (create new row, navigate to its detail), and open-detail actions. Adds a detail view that loads one existing row by id for editing. Edit saves update the existing row. Copy creates a new row with the same meal content, a new identity, and logged_at set to current time, then navigates to the copied row's detail view. This slice introduces the first meal-level read interface, the first update mutation, the first delete mutation, and a third shell navigation item.

classification.why_application: Entry management encodes FoodTracker-specific domain semantics: the distinction between creating a meal and editing an existing one, copy-and-navigate behavior specific to this UX, hard-delete confirmation semantics, and the reuse of the existing meal validation contract for edits. None of this generalises to a shared platform capability.
non_goals: Search, filtering, sorting controls, or pagination
Undo, soft delete, or audit history
New nutrition fields or schema changes
classification.not_platform: The entry management flow (delete confirmation, copy-and-navigate, edit with existing validation reuse) is specific to the FoodTracker intake domain. No general-purpose CRUD pattern should be extracted to platform from this slice.

EntryDetail.description: Stable response contract for GET /api/food/entries/{id} and POST /api/food/entries/{id}/copy. Used by the frontend to populate the edit form. Not a Dataset — returned as a plain JSON dict.

fields.id: string — UUID of the meal entry row
fields.meal_type: string — one of: breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack, other
fields.dish_name: string — server-derived from items[].name at intake time; read-only for edit
fields.red_meat_g: number (float) — red meat content in grams

serialisation_rules: id serialised as str (UUID hex with hyphens)
logged_at, created_at, updated_at serialised as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS' (naive, no timezone suffix) — consistent with existing logged_at serialisation pattern
kcal and confidence serialised as int
All other numeric fields serialised as float
notes is null when no notes value is stored

EntryEditRequest.description: Stable request contract for PUT /api/food/entries/{id}. Accepts simplified edit payload — dish_name and nutrition fields directly. Does not use the intake items[] flow. Does not require validate_and_normalise reuse. Product decision (Option A) recorded 2026-03-21.

fields.meal_type: string — one of: breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack, other
fields.dish_name: string — user-editable display name for the meal
fields.red_meat_g: number (float) — red meat content in grams

excluded_fields: id — system-managed, must not be submitted
created_at — system-managed, must not be submitted
updated_at — system-managed, must not be submitted
items — not part of this simplified edit contract; intake and edit are separate flows
validation_rules: All numeric fields must be non-negative
meal_type must be one of the allowed enum values
logged_at must be a parseable datetime string
kcal and confidence must be integers
dish_name must be a non-empty string

invariants: No row is written to foodtracker.food_logs unless the user has explicitly confirmed an action (Accept for intake, Save for edit, Confirm for delete, Copy action for copy)
PUT /api/food/entries/{id} uses the EntryEditRequest contract — a simplified edit path separate from the intake flow; it does not invoke validate_and_normalise
PUT /api/food/entries/{id} updates the existing row in-place; it never creates a second row
POST /api/food/entries/{id}/copy always assigns a new uuid4() id to the copied row
POST /api/food/entries/{id}/copy always sets logged_at to server datetime.now() (same time source as used elsewhere in the app)
DELETE /api/food/entries/{id} is a hard delete — the row is permanently removed from foodtracker.food_logs
updated_at is NOT auto-maintained by a database trigger; the PUT endpoint must explicitly set updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP in the UPDATE SQL
id, created_at, and updated_at are system-managed fields and must not be accepted as editable input in PUT or copy payloads
CORS must be expanded to allow DELETE and PUT methods for this slice (current: GET POST only)
dish_name in the edit flow is accepted directly from the user in the PUT body (EntryEditRequest contract); this differs from the intake flow where dish_name is derived server-side from items[].name
The GET /api/food/entries endpoint returns all rows in descending logged_at order (most recent first)
The report endpoint (GET /api/food/report) is strictly read-only — unchanged from Sprint 02
The intake endpoints (POST /api/food/validate, POST /api/food/meals) are unchanged from Sprint 01
failure_modes: VALIDATION_ERROR — PUT body fails EntryEditRequest validation (missing required field, wrong type, invalid enum value); HTTP 422
NOT_FOUND — the requested entry id does not exist in foodtracker.food_logs; HTTP 404 (GET /entries/{id}, PUT, DELETE, copy)
DB_CONSTRAINT — a database CHECK constraint is violated at update or insert time; HTTP 400
INTERNAL_ERROR — unexpected exception caught by install_exception_handlers; HTTP 500
PARSE_ERROR — PUT request body is not syntactically valid JSON; HTTP 422
MISSING_FIELD — a required field is absent in PUT body; HTTP 422
INVALID_FIELD — a field is present but fails type or constraint checks in PUT body; HTTP 422

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/food/entries
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Returns all rows from foodtracker.food_logs as a Dataset conforming to the UI data contract. Rows are ordered by logged_at descending. No filters, no pagination in this slice.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/food/entries/{id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Returns the full editable field set for a single stored meal entry. Used by the frontend to load an existing row into the edit form. Returns ApiError HTTP 404 if id not found.

exposed_surfaces.name: PUT /api/food/entries/{id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Accepts an EntryEditRequest body (simplified edit contract — dish_name and nutrition directly, no items field). Validates and updates the existing row in-place. Returns the updated row as a single-row Dataset. Returns ApiError HTTP 404 if id not found, HTTP 422 on validation failure, HTTP 400 on DB_CONSTRAINT. Does not invoke validate_and_normalise — edit and intake are separate flows (Option A product decision, 2026-03-21).

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/food/entries/{id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Hard-deletes one row from foodtracker.food_logs by id. Returns HTTP 204 No Content on success. Returns ApiError HTTP 404 if id not found.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/food/entries/{id}/copy
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Reads the existing row identified by id, creates a new row with the same meal content fields (all except id, created_at, updated_at), assigns a new uuid4() id, sets logged_at to server datetime.now(). Returns the newly created row as an EntryDetail. Returns ApiError HTTP 404 if source id not found.

internal_flow.name: list_entries
internal_flow.description: GET /api/food/entries: SELECT all columns from foodtracker.food_logs ORDER BY logged_at DESC. Serialise each row to a Dataset row dict. Return Dataset with ENTRIES_OVERVIEW_SCHEMA, DatasetMeta(object_type='food_entry', label='Meal Entries', total=row_count, row_actions=['delete','copy','detail']).

internal_flow.name: get_entry_detail
internal_flow.description: GET /api/food/entries/{id}: SELECT all columns from foodtracker.food_logs WHERE id = %s. If no row found, return ApiError HTTP 404 (NOT_FOUND). Serialise all columns including created_at and updated_at. Return the entry_detail dict directly (not wrapped in Dataset) as JSON HTTP 200.

internal_flow.name: update_entry
internal_flow.description: PUT /api/food/entries/{id}: Parse JSON body as EntryEditRequest (see contracts.named_contracts.EntryEditRequest). Validate required fields and types; on failure return ApiError HTTP 422. Check that id exists in foodtracker.food_logs; if not, return ApiError HTTP 404. Execute UPDATE foodtracker.food_logs SET logged_at=%s, meal_type=%s, dish_name=%s, kcal=%s, protein_g=%s, carbs_g=%s, fat_g=%s, fiber_g=%s, good_fat_g=%s, meat_g=%s, red_meat_g=%s, sodium_mg=%s, confidence=%s, notes=%s, updated_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id=%s RETURNING *. Catch CheckViolation/IntegrityError and return ApiError HTTP 400 DB_CONSTRAINT. Commit. Wrap the returned row in a single-row Dataset with ENTRIES_OVERVIEW_SCHEMA. Return HTTP 200. Note: does NOT call validate_and_normalise — edit and intake are separate flows (Option A).
outputs: Dataset (single updated row, HTTP 200) or ApiError (HTTP 404 / 422 / 400)

internal_flow.name: delete_entry
internal_flow.description: DELETE /api/food/entries/{id}: Execute DELETE FROM foodtracker.food_logs WHERE id = %s. Check cursor.rowcount; if rowcount == 0, the row did not exist — rollback and return ApiError HTTP 404. Commit. Return HTTP 204 No Content. Single-statement approach — no prior SELECT.
outputs: HTTP 204 No Content or NOT_FOUND ApiError (HTTP 404)

internal_flow.name: copy_entry
internal_flow.description: POST /api/food/entries/{id}/copy: SELECT all columns from foodtracker.food_logs WHERE id = %s. If not found, return ApiError HTTP 404. Assign new_id = uuid4(). Set new_logged_at = datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'). INSERT into foodtracker.food_logs with all meal content fields (meal_type, dish_name, kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g, good_fat_g, meat_g, red_meat_g, sodium_mg, confidence, notes) copied from the source row, new_id as id, new_logged_at as logged_at. RETURNING *. Commit. Return the inserted row as entry_detail dict (HTTP 201).

internal_required.role: Persistent storage for foodtracker.food_logs; schema pre-provisioned via migrations/001_init_schema.sql. Sprint 03 reads individual rows, updates rows, deletes rows, and inserts copy rows.

risks.risk: CORS expansion from GET POST to GET POST PUT DELETE
risks.impact: The draft explicitly notes that current CORS allows GET POST only and that the slice must either work within that constraint or deliberately expand. This design deliberately expands CORS. The implementer must update allow_methods in main.py. Failure to do so will cause the browser to block PUT and DELETE requests from the frontend with a CORS preflight failure.

If the PUT endpoint omits the explicit SET updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP in the SQL, the field will remain equal to created_at after updates. The implementer must include it explicitly. This is documented as a known gap from Sprint 02.

risks.risk: Copy uses datetime.now() for logged_at (server local time)
risks.impact: Consistent with the existing server time baseline used elsewhere. No additional risk introduced. Documented for traceability.

risks.risk: PUT body uses simplified EntryEditRequest contract (Option A decision, 2026-03-21)
risks.impact: The PUT body is NOT the intake JSON shape. It accepts dish_name and nutrition fields directly. No items field. No validate_and_normalise call. The frontend form sends the stored dish_name as an editable field. Backend validates EntryEditRequest inline. This is intentional — edit and intake are separate flows. Implementer must not attempt to reuse intake validation logic here.

risks.risk: Race condition between DELETE and concurrent GET /entries
risks.impact: Low risk in a single-user local app. No concurrency handling is required for this slice. Documented for awareness.

open_questions.question: Should the PUT /api/food/entries/{id} body use the intake items[] flow (with validate_and_normalise) or a simplified edit contract?
open_questions.resolution: Option A selected by human (2026-03-21): PUT body accepts dish_name and nutrition fields directly (EntryEditRequest contract). Does NOT require validate_and_normalise reuse for the edit path. Simpler edit form; edit and intake are separate flows.
